title: Enhanced postoperative mobilization and biotracking after colorectal oncological resection (INTENSE-Study)
summary: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the second and third most common cancer in Western countries. The optimal therapy for CRC is individualized and should be assessed by a multidisciplinary team. Prognostically, the most decisive step in this multimodal concept is surgical resection, if indicated. However, perioperative morbidity after colorectal surgery is still relevant and has a negative impact on the long-term oncological outcome of patients. Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) is a multimodal perioperative care pathway originally designed to minimize perioperative stress and accelerate postoperative recovery in patients undergoing colorectal surgery. Early mobilization is one central element in the postoperative ERAS setting; however, evidence regarding effective training goals and specific early mobilization protocols is lacking. Therefore, the purpose of this randomized trial is to evaluate an enhanced postoperative mobilization programme accompanied by activity and biotracking after oncological, minimally invasive colorectal surgery (laparoscopic or robot-assisted) for colorectal carcinoma (CRC). The aim of this trial is to optimize oncological therapy for CRC through enhanced recovery and reduction of morbidity.
conditions: Elective minimally invasive colorectal surgery for CRC

interventions.name: Intervention group: In the intervention group, the patients are instructed to complete the EPM within the established ERAS setting from the day of the operation (POD 0) until the 5th postoperative day (POD 5). The exercise programme consists of two sessions per day and includes breathing and walking

Control group: In the control group, the patients participate in the established ERAS setting without an EPM. These patients also wear activity trackers but with a covered display, and they do not have a target step count.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- All patients scheduled for elective minimally invasive (laparoscopic or robot-assisted) colorectal surgery for CRC 
- no intended multivisceral resection (exceptions are small atypical liver wedge resections, biopsies, abdominal wall resection, partial prostate/bladder resection, adnexectomy, cholecystectomy)
- preoperatively mobile patients (e.g., not wheelchair bound) 
- no contraindication for wearing activity tracker devices
Exclusion criteria:
- primary open surgical technique
